overview.headline: Tracking rising atmospheric carbon dioxide from Mauna Loa to past and future climate

keyPoints.point: Students learn that global average atmospheric carbon dioxide reached 422.8 ppm in 2024, setting a new record high.
keyPoints.quote: global average atmospheric carbon dioxide was 422.8 parts per million (“ppm,” for short) in 2024, a new record high

keyPoints.point: Students learn that carbon dioxide concentrations are rising mostly because fossil fuels burned for energy release ancient carbon.
keyPoints.quote: Carbon dioxide concentrations are rising mostly because of the fossil fuels that people have been burning for energy

keyPoints.point: Students learn that atmospheric carbon dioxide increased by about 0.8 ppm per year on average in the 1960s during early measurements.
keyPoints.quote: In the 1960s, atmospheric carbon dioxide increased by about 0.8 ppm per year on average

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the annual increase accelerated to 2.6 ppm per year in the last decade from 2015 to 2024.
keyPoints.quote: In the last decade (2015-2024), the annual increase has accelerated to 2.6 ppm per year

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the drop in pH called ocean acidification interferes with marine life building shells and skeletons.
keyPoints.quote: This drop in pH is called ocean acidification, and it interferes with the ability of marine life

keyTerms.gloss: gas that absorbs and radiates heat and warms Earth by trapping energy
keyTerms.quote: Carbon dioxide is Earth’s most important long-lived greenhouse gas: a gas that absorbs and radiates heat

keyTerms.gloss: drop in ocean pH that interferes with marine life ability to build shells
keyTerms.quote: This drop in pH is called ocean acidification, and it interferes with the ability of marine life

keyTerms.gloss: fuels such as coal and oil burned for energy that contain carbon from ancient photosynthesis
keyTerms.quote: Carbon dioxide concentrations are rising mostly because of the fossil fuels that people have been burning for energy

keyTerms.gloss: strongest warm phase linked to largest annual carbon dioxide growth and drought
keyTerms.quote: The years with the largest annual carbon dioxide growth tend to be associated with the strongest El Niños

keyTerms.gloss: seasonal highs and lows driven by summer vegetation growth and winter decay
keyTerms.quote: The seasonal cycle of highs and lows (small peaks and valleys) is driven by Northern Hemisphere summer vegetation growth
